subject: greater honeyguide
title: A Blind Newborn Bird Kills Its Nest-Mates With a Hook on Its Beak

scenes.text: This chick is blind, naked and a few days old. It's already a killer.
The greater honeyguide lays its egg in a bee-eater's nest, at the end of an underground tunnel.
Its mother holds the egg an extra day before laying, so her chick hatches first.
Then it uses needle-sharp hooks on the tip of its bill to bite the host's chicks. One to five minutes of biting is enough.
Nobody saw it until scientists buried infrared cameras inside the dark nests.
By about a month old the hooks are gone. The killer flies out looking innocent.

description:
Greater honeyguide chicks hatch inside the underground nests of little bee-eaters, armed with needle-sharp hooks on the tips of their bills.
Cambridge researchers filmed them in total darkness with buried infrared cameras: a few days old and still blind, the chick bites the host chicks, and one to five minutes of biting was enough to kill. The hooks are gone by the time it leaves the nest, about a month later.
Which bird parent do you think has it worst?
first_comment: The same species is famous for leading people to wild honey. Did you know the honeyguide had this side to it?
